question: Is global argmin over all accepted R45A macros required for local correctness, certified progress, or polynomial termination, or may deterministic TRUMP stop at the first independently certified accepted macro?

symbolic_claim.premise: macro_candidate_for_var(F,v) is accepted, its independent replay passes, and acceptance means verified terminal or strict frozen CLV descent
symbolic_claim.conclusion: the scan may stop immediately at that v without inspecting later variables for purposes of local semantic correctness, certified progress, and polynomial trajectory-height composition
symbolic_claim.reason: semantic authority belongs to the selected macro certificate, not to comparison with rejected/unseen candidates; Lemma 3 bounds any sequence of accepted strict-CLV final states polynomially
symbolic_claim.determinism: variables are inspected in canonical increasing order, so first-accepted policy is deterministic

important_boundary: Changing global-best policy to first-accepted changes which later states are reachable. Therefore universal O4 coverage must be established for the first-accepted policy itself; this gate does not transfer O4 from another policy.

execution.algorithm: for each stall, scan variables in canonical order, construct one R45A candidate at a time, stop on first accepted, then independently replay only that selected candidate
execution.pass: all 26 obtain an accepted independently replayed first macro; this is finite regression evidence for the new policy, not universal coverage
